Spent the week reproducing arXiv 2602.03061, an ICML 2026 paper on measuring LLM accuracy more precisely than a plain average. It reports its estimator winning in all 60 model-benchmark cells and never puts an uncertainty interval on any of them, and the words "bootstrap" and "standard error" do not occur in it. Running their simulator unmodified at low model noise, the variance reduction comes out at -0.33, meaning 33% more variance than the plain average, 95% CI [-0.495, -0.185] over 250 runs with their default setting passing as a control. The small aggregate effect their Corollary 4.7 predicts is real, the 60 per-cell wins are not, and four of their five claims held up otherwise.
